title: The First Day
vision: The bus turns onto the bridge.
wake: You open your eyes. You’re at the bus stop. It’s the first day of your new job, and the bus is just arriving.

bus.text: “Are you getting on?” You just saw this bus fall off the bridge. It hasn’t fallen yet.

left.label: Warn everyone
left.past: You warned everyone and Elif got off with you
left.after: Most of them laugh at you. A girl in a yellow coat gets off and walks over: Elif.

right.label: Walk away quietly
right.past: You walked away without warning anyone
right.after: The doors close. A camera at the bus stop sees you walk away.

sirens.text: You hear sirens from the bridge. Your hands are shaking.

left.label: Put your earbuds in
left.past: You put your earbuds in and turned the music up loud
left.after: The noise is gone. You turn the music all the way up.

right.label: Check the news
right.past: You watched the news
right.after: The bridge is on the screen. The bus is in the water.

red-light.text: The café is across the road. The light is red, the road is empty. Someone is running toward you from behind.

left.label: Wait and look
left.past: You waited at the red light
left.after: The man hands you the keys you dropped. You’re too scared to laugh.

right.label: Run across
right.past: You ran the red light
right.after: A truck hits its horn and only just misses you. The man behind you shouts something, but you don’t look back.
variants: Elif grabs your arm and pulls you back. Your earbud falls out. A truck goes past right in front of you. You never heard its horn.
Elif pulls you back by the arm. A truck goes past, very close, horn on. “Are you crazy?” The man behind you shouts something.

cafe.text: Your hands shake and the coffee spills into your shoe. The waiter gives you a cloth.

left.label: Sit until it dries
left.past: You stayed too long in the café and were late for your first day
left.after: You sit for half an hour and calm down. It’s already after nine.

right.label: Leave right away
right.past: Coffee soaked your shoe and you didn’t wait for it to dry
right.after: Nowhere feels safe. You leave with a wet sock.

work-call.text: “It’s your first day. Where are you?”

left.label: Go to work
left.past: You went to work
left.after: “Fourth floor. We’re waiting.” A normal day. Maybe it will help.

right.label: “I’m sick”
right.past: You skipped work
right.after: Silence. “Fine. We’ll talk tomorrow.” His voice is cold.

elif-asks.text: “How did you know? Is something else going to happen today?”

left.label: Tell her what you saw
left.past: You told Elif about the vision
left.after: She doesn’t laugh. She asks for your number. Saying it out loud makes it feel real.

right.label: “Just a feeling”
right.past: You told Elif it was just a feeling, she didn’t believe you and never called
right.after: She doesn’t believe you. She takes your number anyway.

office.who: The man in the grey suit
office.text: It’s the other man who got off the bus. He works at the desk next to yours. “Fourth floor, let’s take the lift.” There’s a torn “out of order” note on the lift door. The stairs are marble.

left.label: Take the lift with him
left.past: You took the broken lift
left.after: The doors close. A loud creak. Then the fourth floor. He laughs: “See?”

right.label: Take the stairs
right.past: You took the office’s marble stairs
right.after: Four floors. He’s waiting at the top with a smile.

badge.text: “Welcome. This is your ID card. You need it for every door.” It hangs on a long strap.

left.label: Wear it round your neck
left.past: You wore your ID card round your neck
left.after: The card hangs on your chest. For the first time, you feel like you belong here.

right.label: Put it in your pocket
right.past: You put the card in your pocket
right.after: Later you can’t find it. You wait at the door for twenty minutes and your boss frowns.

pharmacy.text: Your hands are still shaking. “This will calm you down. Don’t drink alcohol with it, it makes you dizzy.”

left.label: Take it
left.past: You took the calming pills
left.after: Half an hour later your hands stop shaking. Everything feels a bit slow.

right.label: Leave it
right.past: You didn’t take the pills
right.after: You walk home with shaking hands.

lunch.who: The man in the grey suit
lunch.text: “After lunch, can you help me take some boxes down to the archive? It’s in the basement.”

left.label: “Sure”
left.past: You promised to help the man in the grey suit with the boxes
left.after: “Great. They fixed the lift, by the way.”

right.label: “Sorry, I’m busy”
right.past: You didn’t help the man in the grey suit
right.after: His face falls. He goes back to his desk alone.

stairs.text: You live on the twelfth floor. The lift is making a strange noise. The stairs were just washed and they’re shiny.

left.label: Stairs
left.past: You walked up the freshly washed stairs
left.after: Twelve floors. Your legs are shaking, but you made it.

right.label: Lift
right.past: You took the lift
right.after: The doors close and the light goes on and off. Nothing happens.

locked.text: Your pocket is empty. No keys. The neighbour opens her door: “The balconies are next to each other, you can climb over.”

left.label: Climb across
left.past: You climbed between balconies on the twelfth floor
left.after: One step over the gap to the other balcony. You feel dizzy, but you make it.

right.label: Wait for a locksmith
right.past: You waited for the locksmith
right.after: You sit on the stairs for two hours.

railing-first.text: You go out on the balcony for some air. The railing moves under your hand.

left.label: Fix it later
left.past: You left the loose railing as it was
left.after: You have bigger problems today.

right.label: Tape it up
right.past: You taped the railing and thought it was fixed
right.after: You wrap it in tape three times. Now it feels strong. At least it looks strong.

archive.who: The man in the grey suit
archive.text: He has put the boxes in front of the lift. The “out of order” note is gone. “Come on, there’s room for both of us.”

left.label: Get in the lift
left.past: You got in the lift with the boxes

right.label: Carry the boxes down the stairs
right.past: You carried the boxes down the stairs
right.after: “Your choice.” The doors close. You’re on the second floor when something above you snaps.

food.text: You haven’t eaten since morning. The kitchen clock is five minutes fast again. Your mum always set it that way.

left.label: Fry an egg
left.past: You heated oil for an egg
left.after: You turn on the stove. The oil starts to get hot.

right.label: Just drink water
right.past: You didn’t eat all day
right.after: Your stomach hurts, but the stove stays off.

crash.text: A scream of metal, then a loud crash. The lift fell to the bottom. The man in the grey suit was inside.

left.label: Run down and help
left.past: You ran down to the fallen lift
left.after: It’s too late. You will never forget what you see.

right.label: Step back and call 112
right.past: You called 112 from a distance
right.after: Your voice shakes. Your hands are ice cold and you feel sick.

variants: The boxes fall out of your hands onto the stairs. The lift fell to the bottom. The man in the grey suit was inside.

mom.text: She saw the news. “Are you all right? Please pick up!”

left.label: Answer and calm her down
left.past: You forgot the stove while talking to your mum
left.after: You talk for twenty minutes. You both cry.

right.label: Turn off the stove first
right.past: You didn’t answer your mum’s call
right.after: You turn off the stove. When you call back, her voice is shaking.

pan-fire.text: Something is burning. The pan is on fire and the flames are reaching the cooker hood.

left.label: Throw water on it
left.past: You threw water on burning oil

right.label: Cover it and turn it off
right.past: You put a lid on the burning pan
right.after: The fire goes out. You burned your hand, but the flat is OK.

shredder.text: “We’re closing the office. Everyone go home. Before you leave, put these papers through the shredder.”

left.label: Do it fast, all at once
left.past: You leaned over the shredder and pushed the papers in fast
left.after: The machine eats the papers with a loud noise. Done. You go home.

right.label: Leave them and go home now
right.past: You left without doing what your boss asked
right.after: Your boss says something behind you. You pretend not to hear.

sleep.text: You haven’t slept since yesterday. Your eyes are closing.

left.label: Sleep a little
left.past: You slept and dreamed of the bridge
left.after: You dream about the bridge again. You wake up covered in sweat, but your body feels rested.

right.label: Stay awake
right.past: You didn’t sleep all day
right.after: You make coffee and stare at the ceiling.

stairs-late.text: You’re home early. Twelve floors. Today you saw a lift fall.

left.label: Stairs
left.past: You climbed twelve floors on tired legs
left.after: Twelve floors. Your legs are shaking, but you made it.

right.label: Lift
right.past: You took a lift again after seeing one fall
right.after: You hold your breath as the doors close. You close your eyes at every creak.

locked-late.text: Your pocket is empty. No keys. The neighbour opens her door: “The balconies are next to each other. You can climb over.”

left.label: Climb across
left.past: You climbed between balconies on the twelfth floor
left.after: One step over the gap to the other balcony. You scrape your knee, but you make it.

right.label: Wait for a locksmith
right.past: You waited for the locksmith
right.after: You sit on the stairs for two hours.

railing-late.text: You go out on the balcony for some air. The railing moves under your hand.

left.label: Fix it later
left.past: You left the loose railing as it was
left.after: You have bigger problems today.

right.label: Tape it up
right.past: You taped the railing and thought it was fixed
right.after: You wrap it in tape three times. Now it feels strong. At least it looks strong.

lock-up.text: Everything looks dangerous. You want to shut and lock every window and door.

left.label: Lock everything
left.past: You shut and locked every window
left.after: The last window is shut. For the first time, you feel safe.

right.label: Leave them open
right.past: You left the windows open with a storm coming
right.after: The curtains move in the wind. You hear thunder far away.

shower.text: You’re cold and shaking. The bathroom has an old gas water heater with a small blue flame.

left.label: A long, hot shower
left.past: You took a long shower next to the gas heater
left.after: The hot water helps. Steam fills the room.

right.label: A quick, cold shower
right.past: You put the heater right next to the sofa
right.after: You’re freezing. You pull the electric heater close to the sofa.

elif-news.text: “The other man who got off the bus is dead. In a lift. I’m coming over.”

left.label: “Come”
left.past: You asked Elif to come over
left.after: Half an hour later, she is at your door.

right.label: “Don’t, it’s dangerous”
right.past: You kept Elif away
right.after: Seen. No reply.

variants: “Your office is on the news. The lift fell and the man in the grey suit is dead. Are you OK? I’m coming over.”

police.text: “A camera saw you walk away from the bus stop. We need to ask you some questions.”

left.label: “I’ll come tomorrow”
left.past: You promised the police you’d come tomorrow
left.after: They write it down. Your hands are sweaty when you hang up.

right.label: Hang up
right.past: You hung up on the police
right.after: The phone goes quiet. The silence is worse.

blackout.text: The power is out. The fuse box is in the hallway and everything is dark.

left.label: Fix the fuse by hand
left.past: You reached for the fuse box in the dark
left.after: A small spark. Then the lights come on.

right.label: Light a candle and wait
right.past: You lit a candle
right.after: The candle light moves on the walls. It feels calming.

variants: The power is out. The fuse box is in the hallway. Rain came in through the open window and the floor is all wet.

news-list.text: They read the passenger list. Your name is on it. Not as a survivor, as missing.

left.label: Listen to the end
left.past: You listened to the whole passenger list
left.after: Forty-two names. Then the ads.

right.label: Turn it off, pour some wine
right.past: You poured yourself a glass of wine
right.after: The wine burns your throat. It helps a little.

variants: They read the passenger list. Your name is on it, and so is Elif’s. Not as survivors, as missing.

elif-air.text: “I can’t breathe in here. Can we go out for some air?”

left.label: Go out on the balcony
left.past: You went out on the balcony with Elif
left.after: The night is cool. The city is still full of sirens.

right.label: Stay in, open some wine
right.past: You opened a bottle of wine with Elif
right.after: Two glasses. Elif laughs for the first time today.

mom-night.text: “Should I come over? Don’t be alone tonight.”

left.label: “Come”
left.past: You asked your mum to come
left.after: “I’ll be there in half an hour.” You hate that she’s driving this late.

right.label: “Don’t, I’m fine”
right.past: You told your mum you were fine
right.after: She can hear you’re lying, but she says nothing.

night-pill.text: You can’t sleep. There’s one more pill in the box from the pharmacy. “You can take one more in the evening if you need it.”

left.label: Take another one
left.past: You took a second pill in the evening
left.after: You take it. Soon you feel more relaxed.

right.label: Leave it
right.past: You skipped the second pill
right.after: You put the box in a drawer. Your heart is still beating fast.

drowsy.text: Your eyes are closing. The sofa has never looked this soft.

left.label: Lie down on the sofa
left.past: You lay down on the sofa
left.after: When you open your eyes, it’s later. Your neck hurts.

right.label: Stay up, wash your face
right.past: You washed your face to stay awake
right.after: Cold water. You don’t know the face in the mirror.

railing.text: Elif leans on the railing, looking down. “Is this safe?”

left.label: “Come inside, now!”
left.past: You called Elif inside
left.after: She’s angry, but she comes in. Just then the railing falls into the dark.

right.label: Go to her, hug her
right.past: You leaned on the railing to hug Elif

variants: Elif leans on the railing and looks at the tape. “Did you do this? Is it safe?”

door.text: Someone knocks. You look through the peephole: nobody. The heavy wardrobe stands next to the door.

left.label: Open and look
left.past: You opened the door
left.after: Nobody. There’s a ticket for this morning’s bus on the doormat.

right.label: Push the wardrobe against it
right.past: You pushed the wardrobe against the door
right.after: The wardrobe blocks the door. Nobody knocks again.

left.label: “It’s over!” Open the windows, celebrate
left.past: You thought it was midnight and started celebrating
left.after: Cool air hits your face. You start to laugh.

right.label: Check your phone
right.past: You counted the last five minutes second by second
right.after: 23:55. Five more minutes. You count every second.

fourth-floor.title: Fourth Floor
fourth-floor.text: The cable broke at the third floor. The cleaner shouted “Don’t get in!”, but you were late and didn’t stop.
fourth-floor.hint: Your first day went down fast.
fourth-floor.omen: The lift is making a noise.

archive.title: The Archive
archive.text: He said they fixed it. They hadn’t. You saw the note this morning, but you wanted to be nice.
archive.hint: Helping is nice. Stairs are nicer.
archive.omen: Something above the lift is breaking.

shredder.title: The Shredder
shredder.text: When you leaned over, the strap of your ID card got caught in the machine. It didn’t stop. You had worn that card round your neck since the morning.
shredder.hint: The card worked in your pocket too.

horn.title: The Horn
horn.text: You never even heard the truck. The music was all the way up and nobody was there to pull you back.
horn.hint: At least the music was good.

office-stairs.title: Wet Shoe
office-stairs.text: Your legs were still shaking from the run, and the coffee was still in your shoe. Your foot slipped on the office’s marble step.
office-stairs.hint: Sitting down for five minutes wasn’t that hard.

stairs.title: Wet Stairs
stairs.text: You slipped on the seventh floor. The pills made your legs heavy, and the stairs were still wet.
stairs.hint: Stairs are good for you, they say.

balcony.title: The Next Balcony
balcony.text: The gap was bigger than it looked. Halfway over, the pills made you dizzy.
balcony.hint: The neighbour wanted to help. It didn’t help.

kitchen.title: A Glass of Water
kitchen.text: The moment the water hit the oil, the flames hit the ceiling.
kitchen.hint: Your mum was right: never leave the stove on.
kitchen.omen: The oil is getting very hot.

heater-gas.title: The Gas Heater
heater-gas.text: All the windows were closed. The pills made you sleepy, and the gas had no smell.
heater-gas.hint: You locked every door. Death was already inside.

fuse.title: Electric Shock
fuse.text: Rain had covered the hallway floor. In the dark you stood in the water and touched the fuse box.
fuse.hint: Calling an electrician wasn’t that hard.

last-glass.title: The Last Glass
last-glass.text: The pharmacist had warned you: no alcohol. The evening pill and the wine. Your breathing slowed, then stopped.
last-glass.hint: Reading the label takes three seconds.

fell-asleep.title: Fast Asleep
fell-asleep.text: Your eyes closed on the sofa. The blanket touched the heater, or the candle. Nobody was there to wake you.
fell-asleep.hint: You stayed awake all day and slept at the wrong moment.

railing.title: The Railing
railing.text: You held her. The railing couldn’t hold you both.
railing.hint: You said you’d fix it later.

wardrobe.title: The Wardrobe
wardrobe.text: It was the police. They came because you hung up on them. They broke the door open and the wardrobe fell on you.
wardrobe.hint: Talking to them would have taken ten minutes.

curtain.title: The Curtain
curtain.text: The kitchen clock was five minutes fast. You opened all the windows at once, and the wind blew the candle onto the curtain.
curtain.hint: Your mum always set the clocks fast. Always.

panic-street.title: Frozen
panic-street.text: You froze in the middle of the road. You never saw the cyclist.
panic-street.hint: Your fear was bigger than everything. Even the cyclist.

panic-home.title: Panic
panic-home.text: You couldn’t breathe and ran for the door. You tripped at the top of the stairs.
panic-home.hint: You ran from death, but not from yourself.

panic-work.title: The Glass Door
panic-work.text: You couldn’t breathe. You ran at the office’s glass door without seeing it.

collapse-street.title: The Pavement
collapse-street.text: You collapsed on the pavement. People thought you were drunk. Nobody stopped.
collapse-street.hint: You should have looked after yourself.

collapse-home.title: The Kitchen Counter
collapse-home.text: You felt dizzy in the kitchen and hit your head on the counter.
collapse-home.hint: No food, no sleep, no rest.

collapse-work.title: The Office Stairs
collapse-work.text: Your legs gave up on the office stairs.

together.title: You Both Made It
together.text: 00:00. Elif says nothing, and neither do you. Today death missed two people.
together.hint: Tomorrow you’ll both wake up. That’s all.

alone.title: Midnight, Alone
alone.text: 00:00. You’re alive. You saved no one, but you’re here. Death was wrong.
